title: Docker Examples
description: Small Docker examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Images and containers
examples.description: An image is a packaged starting point. A container is a running or stopped instance created from an image.

examples.title: Run a small example
examples.description: docker run creates and starts a container. --rm asks Docker to remove that container after it exits.

examples.title: See local images
examples.description: An image list shows packages stored on your machine. A tag is a readable label for an image version.

examples.title: List containers
examples.description: docker ps lists running containers. Adding -a also shows stopped containers that were not automatically removed.

examples.title: Name a practice container
examples.description: A container name gives you a clear target for later inspection. The -d option runs it in the background.

examples.title: Read container logs
examples.description: Logs record messages written by a container's program. They help explain what it is doing or why it stopped.

examples.title: Inspect container details
examples.description: inspect returns detailed configuration and state. A format expression can select a small part of the result.

examples.title: Read a Dockerfile
examples.description: A Dockerfile describes how to build an image. FROM chooses a base; COPY adds a file from the build folder.

examples.title: Build a local image
examples.description: docker build reads a Dockerfile and its build context. -t gives the resulting image a tag.

examples.title: Keep unwanted files out
examples.description: A .dockerignore file excludes matching files from the build context. This keeps temporary or private files out of a build.

examples.title: Volumes store data outside a container
examples.description: A volume is storage managed separately from a container's writable layer. It can outlive a particular container.
examples.code:
Container A writes a note to a named volume
Container A is removed
Container B mounts the same volume and reads the note

examples.title: Stop and remove only your practice container
examples.description: Cleanup should target the exact resource you created. Stopping a container is separate from removing it.
examples.code:
docker stop club-web
docker rm club-web
